diagnosis.original_question: Whether v179's giant water polygons came from mesh coverage, geometric normals, or the capture renderer.
diagnosis.unlit_control_result: With HLOD proxies present, the uniform source-water material alternated against stale proxy/terrain representations. Isolating all HLOD primitives produced a continuous median-water silhouette.
diagnosis.root_cause: WorldPartition->LoadAllActors loaded source actors and their instanced HLOD proxies together. The raw editor-world scene capture could draw both, unlike runtime World Partition. A transient source-only material override therefore produced a mixed-material polygon mosaic.
diagnosis.corrected_inference: v179 does not prove discontinuous geometric normals or inadequate water tessellation. Its visible polygons were capture contamination from simultaneous source and HLOD representations; the removed material candidate remains unaccepted because it was never reviewed through a valid exclusive capture path.

automation.editor_source_line_limit: RaftSimEditorSouthForkFullReach.cpp is 2999 lines and within the 3000-line guard

renderer_evidence.pixel_comparison_scope: No runtime art changed. Small whole-frame deltas reflect removal of duplicate HLOD/source rendering plus ordinary temporal renderer variation.
renderer_evidence.visual_decision: technical capture correction accepted; photoreal acceptance unchanged

accepted: Settled source captures now enforce the same source-or-HLOD exclusivity that runtime World Partition applies.
The configured median flow band is selected at component level, so editor-world capture no longer depends on HiddenInGame semantics.
All 185 HLOD primitives and 41 inactive flow-band components are restored after capture; no package, map, material, mesh, hydraulic field, collision, navigation, or gameplay authority changes.
The corrected five-view evidence shows a continuous water surface and invalidates v179's geometric-normal conclusion.
rejected_or_open: v180 is an evidence-correctness improvement, not a photoreal water upgrade; the visual output remains essentially the accepted v169 baseline.
Water remains too dark, uniform, low-volume, and procedurally rippled, with insufficient breaking crests, entrained-air volume, turbulence, spray, and shoreline integration at named rapids.
Terrain, vegetation, rock, infrastructure, characters, raft presentation, animation, lighting, and release media remain below final photoreal acceptance.
No named guide, art, geospatial, legal, marketing, or release-media reviewer has approved this evidence.
